summary: The week split cleanly in two: a 55-hour interactive burst (2026-09-13 to 2026-09-15 21:35Z, your approved full-cycle run) that landed six new FINAL verdicts (GD, WSP.TO, WTW, NVT, BDX, AON, all WATCH) taking the campaign to 20 total FINAL dives, then roughly four days of near-total silence while the campaign stayed PAUSED for that same session, which the routine's own commit history says went idle after 21:35Z on the 15th. Eighteen consecutive campaign stand-down fires since have found no further campaign-stage work, escalated to you by push notification twice (2026-09-17 21:12Z, 2026-09-18 00:12Z) and again this morning (06:12Z), all unanswered as of this digest. Two structural changes landed in the burst worth knowing about even though they read like plumbing: every OVER_CROWDED heat call now writes a shadow row (81 on the book, up from 1), and a link with a priced instrument (hormuz-maritime's freight-futures fund, BWET) now scores separately from the operating companies sitting on it. Separately, CI went red the moment the burst landed (2026-09-14) and stayed red for four days until you fixed it yourself on 2026-09-18 (three commits: a ledger-counter lag rule, a page-size cap, an identifier-masking fix). No new INVESTABLE this week: ACM stays the only one. Radar is still PAUSED, unchanged since 2026-09-01.

ranked.title: WSP.TO: the first admission_lapse ever recorded, and it was the audit that failed, not the analysis
ranked.case: This dive drafted INVESTABLE and its fresh-context red team upheld that verdict, independently reproducing the entry zone to within rounding. Hours later the same day, a separate fresh-context placement audit failed the underlying mapping on role_mismatch: WSP's own data-center services page now 403s the fetcher, and the replacement source (an Industrial Info Resources article) never uses the words permit, environmental, or site-select anywhere in its stored text, only naming WSP on general construction and engineering work. Rather than delete a real verdict or leave it silently misstating its support, the new admission_lapse mechanism downgraded it to WATCH while keeping the file FINAL and printing exactly what would restore it: an official source that names WSP's permitting role specifically, followed by a fresh PASS audit and re-selection to O1. The would_buy_zone is unchanged from the pre-lapse entry_zone; what caps this one at WATCH is the audit, not the numbers.

ranked.title: GD (General Dynamics) closed the 30-hour stall from last week's digest
ranked.case: Last week's #4 item was GD stuck BLOCKED for 30 hours across 11 routine fires on a failing mapping audit with no placement-level substitute. This week's interactive session ran a fresh-context universe-audit pass directly, fixed the underlying evidence gap, got a PASS placement audit, and carried GD through deepdive and red team to FINAL WATCH the same day (2026-09-13-14). The red team's pre-mortem is honest about what would make this wrong: sustained European and allied rearmament demand rolling over faster than the disclosed multi-year backlog implies, which the file cannot rule out from here.

ranked.title: NVT and BDX: the two names you specifically asked for both landed as WATCH
ranked.case: Your 2026-09-15 call ("Yes, dive NVT and BDX") used the new per-theme O1 cap exception to add a 4th O1 slot to ai-infrastructure and glp1-fill-finish. Both closed FINAL WATCH grade B. NVT's gap is real but the zone is drawn conservatively: the market's 43.19% five-year implied FCF CAGR sits well above even this dive's own 19.26% base case, and the would-buy band ($51.01-$58.41) is built on a bear case anchored above nVent's own trailing growth rather than a demonstrated floor. BDX's red team flagged a live gap the zone does not stress: the bear-case floor is conditioned on operating performance alone and does not model the unquantified legal and product-remediation addbacks already disclosed in the earnings-quality grade.

ranked.title: AON and WTW: hormuz-maritime's broker link gets its second and third names, and the new broker exception fires for real
ranked.case: Both dives sit on specialty-marine-broking, the same link as ESLT's naval-escort neighbor. AON closed grade B with a defended would-buy zone built on the debt-service drag from its own disclosed $17.0B acquisition financing. WTW is the first FINAL dive to actually use the 2026-09-15 broker quality exception: its Piotroski and Beneish scores are structurally NOT_APPLICABLE (an insurance broker's income statement carries no cost-of-revenue line to compute them from), and the earnings-quality grade is null with that reason named rather than defaulted to a silent pass, which per method section 7 still caps the verdict at WATCH exactly as any other null grade would.
